yes.t: ==A light, non-heavy hit of moisture== in the morning, good on normal to dry and combination skin.

no.title: Little visible payoff
no.t: ==Little visible change in tone or firmness==; early lift can fade after about six weeks.

no.title: Can sting
no.t: ==Stings on some faces==, even on a first try.

sunday-riley-u-f-o-acne-treatment-face-o.bottom: A salicylic acid and tea tree face oil for breakout-prone skin, used as a spot treatment or all over. Many see bumps shrink fast without dryness. It has a strong scent, a steep price and breaks some people out.

yes.title: Shrinks spots fast
yes.t: Used as a spot dab or all over, ==bumps look smaller by morning and calmer within weeks==.

yes.title: Not drying
yes.t: Unlike many salicylic products, ==it leaves dry and combination skin soft==, with no flaking.

yes.title: Deep, stubborn spots
yes.t: Seems to ==quiet congested pores and deep spots that other products left==.

yes.title: Fine for many reactive faces
yes.t: Sensitive, breakout-prone skin ==often takes it well==, and some use it every morning.

no.title: Strong medicinal smell
no.t: Not fragrance-free: ==a cumin-like, menthol scent that fades in about 15 minutes==.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Brings up ==chin and cheek bumps== on some skin.

no.title: Pricey for a small bottle
no.t: A ==steep price for a small bottle==, and some drop it for cheaper salicylic acid.

no.title: Nothing for some faces
no.t: ==No visible change for some even after three months==; results depend on skin type.

supergoop-bright-eyed-mineral-eye-cream-.bottom: A fragrance-free tinted mineral SPF eye cream that brightens under-eyes. It is thick, pricey and irritates some eyes.

yes.title: Brightens under-eyes
yes.t: The tint ==lifts dark circles and looks awake for hours== with no other makeup.

no.title: Can irritate the eyes
no.t: ==Stings or irritates the eye area== for some, so patch test first.

no.title: Thick, pastes under concealer
no.t: Feels ==heavy and paste-like==, and can pill under concealer.

supergoop-every-single-face-watery-lotio.bottom: A scented, watery SPF 50 that leaves a glow with no white cast. It can sting or itch, and the scent is strong for some.

yes.title: Clear finish with a glow
yes.t: Rubs in ==without any white cast== and dries to a soft glow.

yes.title: Weightless, non-greasy
yes.t: ==Melts in and doesn't pill==, with a light, non-greasy feel.

no.title: Can sting or itch
no.t: ==Burned the eyes or itched by day's end== for some sensitive faces.

no.title: Noticeable scent
no.t: A ==noticeable scent that is too strong for some noses==.

supergoop-glowscreen-spf-40.bottom: A tinted, pearly SPF 40 sunscreen that doubles as a glowy primer under makeup. It is fragrance-free and suits dry to normal skin and deeper tones. Pale skin can turn orange, and it breaks some people out.

yes.title: Glowy makeup primer
yes.t: ==Sits smoothly under foundation== and gives a lit-from-within finish by day.

yes.title: No ashy cast on deeper skin
yes.t: Tan to deep tones get ==a pearly glow instead of an ashy cast==, with little white residue.

yes.title: Stands in for tinted moisturizer
yes.t: The tint ==can replace foundation or tinted moisturizer== when the shade matches your skin.

yes.title: Hydrating on many dry faces
yes.t: A ==dewy, moisturized feel== that lasts instead of drying down flat.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Bumps ==show up after days to months of wear==, even on skin that rarely breaks out.

no.title: Orange on fair skin
no.t: ==Reads orange or too dark on pale skin==, and a metallic cast shows in the original shade.

tip.t: Blend a small amount into plain sunscreen or a lighter base to soften the tint.

alt.t: Unseen, the untinted option, if the tint runs dark or looks slick on you.

no.title: Very shiny worn alone
no.t: Alone it can look ==greasy and mirror-shiny==, and it can show up pores and texture.

tip.t: Keep it for under makeup or over another sunscreen, not as a solo layer.

no.title: Pills over some moisturizers
no.t: ==Pills or streaks over some creams==, especially water-based or gel-cream layers.

supergoop-mineral-mattescreen-spf-40.bottom: A fragrance-free tinted mineral SPF 40 with a silky primer feel and a true matte finish. It suits oily, combination and sensitive skin best. The tint can look ashy on deeper skin, and it's pricey for the size.

yes.title: A true matte finish
yes.t: ==Oil control lasts through the day== even in humid heat.

yes.title: Works like a primer
yes.t: Makeup ==stays put over it==, and it blurs pores on its own.

yes.title: Gentle on sensitive skin
yes.t: ==Reactive skin stays calm over years of use== with no stinging.

yes.title: Tint softens white cast
yes.t: The ==tint settles into light and medium skin tones== instead of showing as chalk.

no.title: Tint can look ashy
no.t: ==Deeper skin tones can see a visible hue== that doesn't blend away, or looks too light in summer.

no.title: Can feel drying
no.t: ==Wears dry without moisturizer underneath==, though some never get dry patches.

no.title: Sits like a silicone layer
no.t: ==Needs extra rubbing to blend== and can pill under makeup.

no.title: Pricey for the size
no.t: ==A premium price for a small tube==, next to cheaper mineral options.

supergoop-play-everyday-lotion-spf-50.bottom: A citrus-scented SPF 50 lotion that wears hydrating with a dewy finish. It can look shiny and may irritate a few faces.

yes.title: Moisturizer-like on dry skin
yes.t: Dry skin can ==skip a separate moisturizer==, and it still feels light.

yes.title: No grey cast on deeper skin
yes.t: Rubs in clear, ==without a grey cast even on deeper skin tones==.

yes.title: Mostly kind to the eyes
yes.t: ==Doesn't sting the eyes for most==, unlike many chemical sunscreens.

yes.title: Smooth under makeup
yes.t: Works ==as a primer under makeup== without pilling for most.

no.title: Shiny, sticky on skin
no.t: Leaves ==a shiny, slightly sticky finish== that suits sport better than everyday wear.

no.title: Citrus scent
no.t: An essential-oil citrus scent, ==mild to some and strong to others==, that fades.

no.title: Itchy or hot spots for some
no.t: Hot, itchy spots or hives ==can appear within a week of daily use==.

no.title: Stings if sweat runs in
no.t: Can ==burn the eyes when sweat carries it in==, and it is not sweatproof.

supergoop-superscreen-hydrating-daily-cr.bottom: A fragrance-free SPF 40 cream that works like a daily moisturizer. It suits dry and sensitive skin. It is expensive, and a few faces broke out or burned.

yes.title: Moisturizer-like sunscreen
yes.t: Feels ==more like a daily moisturizer than a sunscreen==, with no chalky cast.

yes.title: Calm on sensitive skin
yes.t: Many ==dry, sensitive faces had no reaction== and a natural glow.

no.title: Breaks out or burns some
no.t: Felt heavy and ==caused breakouts or burning on some faces==.

no.title: Pricey for daily use
no.t: Costs ==a lot for how fast a daily face and neck layer goes==.

supergoop-unseen-sunscreen-spf-50.bottom: A clear, silicone-feel SPF 50 gel that works like a makeup primer, with no white cast. It suits oily skin; it stings some eyes, and pills or feels greasy on others.

yes.title: Primer-like under makeup
yes.t: A ==smooth, primer-like layer under makeup== with a velvety finish.

yes.title: Clear, no white cast
yes.t: Stays ==invisible on brown and deep skin==, not just on fair tones.

yes.title: Weightless and matte on oily skin
yes.t: Feels ==weightless and stays matte on many oily and combination faces==.

yes.title: Easy on some reactive skin
yes.t: ==Doesn't irritate some very reactive faces==, even ones that flush with other sunscreens.

no.title: Burns the eyes
no.t: Often ==burns if it gets into the eyes==, its most common catch.

no.title: Pills over other products
no.t: The silicone layer ==pills or peels off over skincare and makeup== for some.

no.title: Greasy or shiny for some
no.t: Feels ==greasy and silicone-heavy== to some, and shiny in heat.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: ==Clogs pores with whiteheads== or breakouts for some.

tatcha-the-dewy-skin-cream.bottom: A rich, scented cream that gives dry skin plush moisture and a dewy glow, best at night or in winter. It's too heavy for oily skin and breaks some people out. The price is high.

yes.title: Rich moisture for dry skin
yes.t: A thick cream that ==keeps very dry skin plump overnight==; a little goes a long way.

yes.title: Dewy glow that lasts
yes.t: Skin looks ==soft and luminous for hours==, and makeup sets well over it.

yes.title: Comfortable on dry, reactive skin
yes.t: ==Stays calm on many dry, very reactive faces==, even through flares.

yes.title: Offsets retinoid dryness
yes.t: Over a retinoid at night it ==takes the edge off the flaking and tightness==.

no.title: Too heavy for oily skin
no.t: Feels ==thick, greasy and shiny on oily or combination skin==, and worse in warm weather.

tip.t: Save it for night or winter and use a thin layer.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: ==Closed comedones and cystic breakouts== appear for some, even on dry skin.

no.title: Strong added fragrance
no.t: Has added fragrance that ==bothers some very reactive skin==, though others barely notice it.

no.title: Pricey for what it does
no.t: ==A premium price for a moisturizer==, and several stopped repurchasing it.

tatcha-the-rice-wash.bottom: A creamy rice-powder cleanser with fine polishing grains and a light floral scent. It suits dry, reactive and combination skin; a pea-size amount goes far. The price and scent put some off.

yes.title: Cleans without drying
yes.t: Rinses clean and leaves skin ==soft and hydrated, with no tight feeling== even on very dry skin.

yes.title: Comfortable on reactive skin
yes.t: ==Tolerated by very sensitive skin that stings with other washes==, morning and night.

yes.title: Gentle polishing
yes.t: The grains are ==fine and soft==, smoothing without a scrubby feel.

yes.title: A little goes far
yes.t: A ==pea-size amount lathers well== and a bottle lasts for months.

no.title: Strips or dries some skin
no.t: Some skin ==still feels tight or flaky after a few weeks==, dry types included.

tip.t: Use it as the second step after a balm or oil cleanse.

no.title: Added fragrance
no.t: Contains ==added fragrance==, which smells too strong for some reactive skin.

no.title: Pricey for a cleanser
no.t: At this cost it ==feels little different from a drugstore cleanser== to some.

no.title: Brings on pimples for a few
no.t: ==Tiny pimples or closed comedones== appeared in some after a few weeks.

tatcha-the-silk-sunscreen-spf-50.bottom: A mineral SPF 50 with 10% zinc oxide and a silky, satin finish that blends without a white cast. It sits well under makeup. The bottle leaks and flakes, and the price is high.

yes.title: Blends in with no white cast
yes.t: ==Rubs in clear, even on brown skin==, which is rare for a mineral SPF.

yes.title: Smooth base under makeup
yes.t: Sits ==like a primer under foundation and concealer== without caking.

yes.title: Weightless satin glow
yes.t: Dries fast to a ==soft satin glow== that holds up in hot, humid weather.

no.title: Leaky, flaking bottle
no.t: The ==packaging spills in a bag and the paint flakes off== the bottle.

no.title: Costs more than most
no.t: ==A premium price==, hard to justify for a simple mineral SPF.

no.title: Flakes or stains for some
no.t: Can ==dry out or flake on a few faces==, and may stain clothes.

tatcha-the-water-cream.bottom: A light, scented gel cream for oily and combination skin, at its best by day under makeup. Dry skin usually needs something richer, and it's a high price for a simple moisturizer.

yes.title: Light, sinks in fast
yes.t: A watery gel that ==melts in without an oily finish==.

yes.title: Made for oily and combo skin
yes.t: ==Daytime moisture for oily and combination skin==, with less midday shine.

yes.title: Great under makeup
yes.t: A slight tack that ==helps foundation sit smoothly==.

no.title: Not enough for dry skin
no.t: ==Leaves dry skin tight by midday==, even with a second layer.

tip.t: Wear it by day and switch to a richer cream at night or in winter.

alt.t: The richer Tatcha cream, for dry skin or winter nights.

no.title: Splits breakout-prone skin
no.t: Opinion splits on breakout-prone skin: ==it clears some faces and breaks others out==.

no.title: Pricey for what it does
no.t: ==A premium price for a fairly basic==, silicone-heavy formula.

no.title: Has added fragrance
no.t: A ==light floral scent==, which has irritated some reactive skin.

the-inkey-list-10-azelaic-acid-serum.bottom: A fragrance-free 10% azelaic acid serum that soaks in quickly and suits red, breakout-prone skin. Results build over weeks. It pills if layered too soon and breaks some people out.

yes.title: Calmer-looking redness and marks
yes.t: Redness and marks left by blemishes ==look calmer over weeks==.

yes.title: Fewer new breakouts
yes.t: New breakouts ==appear less often== within the first weeks for some.

yes.title: Smoother than The Ordinary's
yes.t: Feels ==smoother, with less pilling and irritation== than The Ordinary's azelaic acid.

yes.title: Soothing for many reactive faces
yes.t: Soaks in fast, and ==the calming feel suits reactive skin== best.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Brings ==breakouts that don't settle== for some, even eased in slowly on sensitive skin.

no.title: Pills if rushed
no.t: Can ==roll off under moisturizer or SPF==, even on bare skin for some.

tip.t: Wait 10 to 15 minutes before layering, and shake it if it separates.

no.title: Results vary
no.t: Some see ==little change after weeks== and reach for a stronger azelaic acid.

no.title: Can peel or irritate
no.t: ==Peels or irritates== some skin, even when built up slowly.

the-inkey-list-10-niacinamide-serum.bottom: A fragrance-free 10% niacinamide serum with a nicer feel than many rivals. It hydrates and suits dry skin. It breaks out or irritates some faces, so start with a small amount.

yes.title: Nicer feel than The Ordinary
yes.t: Sits ==smoother and less sticky than The Ordinary's niacinamide==, with similar results.

yes.title: Hydrating and light
yes.t: Slightly thicker than a water serum, so ==it moisturizes as well as hydrates==.

no.title: Breaks out or irritates some
no.t: ==Tiny bumps and itchy red spots== appeared on some faces within days.

tip.t: Use less and ease in rather than going twice a day.

no.title: Splits opinion on oil control
no.t: Helps ==T-zone oil for some and does little for others==.

the-inkey-list-beta-hydroxy-acid-bha-ser.bottom: A cheap fragrance-free 2% salicylic leave-on with hyaluronic acid. It is gentler than most BHAs, even on dry, sensitive skin. Results are mixed for breakout-prone skin.

yes.title: Exfoliates without drying
yes.t: A leave-on BHA that ==stays comfortable on dry, sensitive skin== used a few times a week.

yes.title: Smoother skin, fewer spots
yes.t: Texture looks ==smoother and spots settle faster== within a few weeks.

no.title: Purging or no change for some
no.t: ==A rough purge, or no visible effect== after weeks, for some breakout-prone skin.

no.title: Can feel sticky
no.t: Slightly thick and ==tacky as a leave-on layer==.

the-inkey-list-bio-active-ceramide-moist.bottom: A fragrance-free ceramide cream that absorbs well for its richness. Dry and sensitive skin like it, but it can feel heavy in hot weather.

yes.title: Hydrating without pilling
yes.t: Rich but ==absorbs fast, with no pilling under makeup==.

yes.title: Calm on irritated skin
yes.t: Skin ==looks less red and tight after a few weeks==.

no.title: Heavy in hot weather
no.t: Feels thick at first, and ==too heavy for some in hot weather==.

the-inkey-list-caffeine-eye-cream.bottom: A light, fragrance-free caffeine gel-cream that perks up puffy morning eyes. Dark circles change slowly or not at all. It does nothing for some, and a few get stinging.

yes.title: De-puffs tired eyes
yes.t: Under-eyes look ==less puffy and more awake after morning use==.

yes.title: Light, cooling hydration
yes.t: A cooling gel-cream that ==hydrates thirsty under-eyes without feeling heavy==.

yes.title: Cheap, easy to repurchase
yes.t: Costs little, and ==a tube lasts around three months== of daily use.

no.title: Nothing special for some
no.t: ==No visible change for some even after weeks==; it feels like a plain moisturiser.

no.title: Dark circles barely move
no.t: ==Dark circles ease only slowly, if at all==; years of use for hereditary ones.

no.title: Can sting or irritate
no.t: Stings on application and ==feels harsh around the eyes== for some.

the-inkey-list-glycolic-acid-toner.bottom: A fragrance-free 10% glycolic toner that is on the strong side. It can work for texture when used sparingly. Many get stinging or redness.

yes.title: Works on texture when sparing
yes.t: Used ==every other day or less it smooths pores and tone== for some.

no.title: Strong, stings
no.t: ==Stinging, redness and a damaged-feeling barrier== for many, even twice weekly.

no.title: Breakouts early on
no.t: ==A bout of breakouts== can follow in the first weeks.

the-inkey-list-hyaluronic-acid-serum.bottom: A fragrance-free, watery hyaluronic serum that feels light and far less sticky than most. It plumps dry skin best under a moisturiser. It breaks some people out, and used alone it can leave skin flaky.

yes.title: Less tacky than rivals
yes.t: ==Smoother and less sticky than The Ordinary's version==, and it does not pill under other products.

yes.title: Soft, plump skin
yes.t: A watery gel that ==leaves skin soft and plump, mostly on dry skin== under a moisturiser.

yes.title: Won't make skin oily
yes.t: ==Hydrates without adding shine or a heavy feel==, which suits oily skin.

yes.title: Cheap and goes far
yes.t: Costs little for a serum, and ==a few drops cover the whole face==.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: ==Small bumps and red pimples can appear within days==, even on skin that had been clear.

no.title: Dries skin used alone
no.t: ==On its own it can leave skin tight or flaky==, so it needs a cream on top.

tip.t: Apply to damp skin and sandwich it between other layers.

no.title: Can irritate a weak barrier
no.t: ==Redness, itching or slight burning== can show up on already damaged skin.

no.title: Awkward bottle
no.t: The bottle has no dropper, so ==product dries around the lid and pouring is messy==.

the-inkey-list-oat-cleansing-balm.bottom: A fragrance-free oat cleansing balm that melts makeup and sunscreen, best as a first cleanse. It suits dry and sensitive skin. It often leaves a film, can separate in the tube and breaks some people out.

yes.title: Soothing on dry, sensitive skin
yes.t: A ==non-stripping, calming first cleanse== that dry and reactive skin tolerates well.

yes.title: Melts makeup and sunscreen
yes.t: Lifts face makeup and ==mineral sunscreen with little rubbing== before the second wash.

yes.title: Leaves dry skin soft
yes.t: Skin feels ==soft and moisturized after rinsing==, and it works as a short hydrating mask.

yes.title: Cheap and lasts a while
yes.t: A tube ==lasts for months at a low price==, well below pricier balms.

no.title: Leaves a waxy film
no.t: Often ==survives the rinse, greasy and waxy==, so a second cleanser is a must.

tip.t: Emulsify it with wet hands, then follow with a gentle water-based cleanser.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Brings on ==clogged pores and breakouts for some==, more often without a second cleanse.

no.title: Separates and varies by tube
no.t: The oil can ==separate in the tube and the texture changes between batches==, sometimes grainy.

tip.t: Warm the tube in your hands first, as it is nearly unusable when cold.

no.title: Gritty oat bits bother some skin
no.t: Hard oat granules ==scratch or irritate sensitive skin== for some.

the-inkey-list-omega-water-cream.bottom: A light, fragrance-free gel cream with niacinamide and ceramides. It suits normal, combination and sensitive skin. It can fall short on dry skin in cold weather.

yes.title: Light, fast absorbing
yes.t: A watery gel that ==sinks in quickly and leaves a soft, slightly dewy finish==.

yes.title: Hydrates without irritating
yes.t: ==Enough moisture for normal to sensitive skin== without redness or itching.

no.title: Too light for dry, cold days
no.t: ==Runs out of steam on dry skin== or in very cold weather.

no.title: Greasy on very oily skin
no.t: On very oily skin it can ==turn slimy or greasy and clog pores==.

the-inkey-list-pha-toner.bottom: A fragrance-free, low-strength PHA toner that gently smooths and softens skin. It suits sensitive and dry skin best, a few nights a week at first. It stings some faces and does little for stubborn texture.

yes.title: Mild exfoliation for sensitive skin
yes.t: A ==mild PHA exfoliant that dry, sensitive skin often tolerates==, daily or every other night.

yes.title: Softer, calmer-looking skin
yes.t: Skin looks ==softer and less red within a week or two== for those who tolerate it.

yes.title: Hydrating, not drying
yes.t: Light and watery, it ==leaves skin hydrated rather than dry or tight==.

no.title: Stings on first use
no.t: ==Tingles or burns on application== for some, even though it is meant to be mild.

no.title: Too mild for stubborn texture
no.t: At a low strength, it ==does little for blackheads or rough texture==.

no.title: Pinkness that lingers
no.t: Can leave ==pinkness lasting a day or two==, or irritation after weeks of steady use.

the-inkey-list-polyglutamic-acid-serum.bottom: A fragrance-free, gel-like hydrating serum that leaves skin soft and plump. The smell is odd and the thick feel is not for everyone.

yes.title: Plump, soft hydration
yes.t: Leaves skin ==soft and plump== on dry skin, best on damp skin.

yes.title: Easy on skin
yes.t: ==Didn't irritate== even after exfoliating, including skin that reacted to hyaluronic acid.

no.title: Odd chemical smell
no.t: Smells ==like glue or cleaner== straight from the pump, though it fades fast.

no.title: Thick gel feel
no.t: Feels ==viscous, silicone-like or cloggy== for some, more primer than serum.

the-inkey-list-retinol-eye-cream.bottom: A fragrance-free, mild retinol eye cream that most tolerate when built up slowly. Visible results are modest, and some get tiny white bumps or irritation around the eyes.

yes.title: Mild for a retinol
yes.t: Light and ==easy on the eye area when built up slowly==, with little redness or dryness.

yes.title: Pairs with other retinoids
yes.t: Fine for ==every-other-night use alongside tretinoin or retinol== on the rest of the face.

no.title: Tiny bumps for some
no.t: Some get ==tiny white bumps under the eyes==, even with small amounts.

no.title: Burns or swells for some
no.t: Can leave eyes ==swollen, burning or very dry==, mostly with daily use from day one.

tip.t: Start twice a week and build up to every other night.

the-inkey-list-salicylic-acid-cleanser.bottom: A low-cost, fragrance-free salicylic acid cleanser for breakout-prone, oily and combination skin. It smooths clogged pores for most; some skin turns dry, or breaks out.

yes.title: Smooths clogged pores
yes.t: Small whiteheads and nose blackheads ==fade within weeks== of daily use.

yes.title: Milder than some acid washes
yes.t: Often cleans ==without a stripped, tight feel==, and some use it twice a day.

yes.title: Go-to in a flare-up
yes.t: Reached for ==when a usual routine stops working== during a flare-up.

yes.title: Low-cost acid step
yes.t: An easy, ==low-cost way to try salicylic acid== without adding a leave-on.

no.title: Drying for some
no.t: Can leave skin ==dry, tight or red==, especially with daily morning use.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: New pimples ==appeared within days to weeks== for a few, including dry, sensitive skin.

no.title: Rinse-off acid does less
no.t: Rinse-off contact is short, so ==it does less than leave-on acid== for congested pores.

no.title: Sharp smell in some bottles
no.t: A pungent chemical smell ==showed up in some bottles==, sometimes with a rash.

the-inkey-list-succinic-acid-treatment.bottom: A cheap fragrance-free spot treatment with succinic acid and sulfur. It suits small, new spots on sensitive skin. Big, painful ones respond slowly.

yes.title: Calms small spots fast
yes.t: On a new spot, ==it brings it to a head and shrinks it within a few uses==, leaving no residue under makeup.

yes.title: Gentle, not drying
yes.t: ==Skin tolerates repeat dabs== without flaking, even sensitive skin and layered with retinol.

no.title: Slow on deep, painful spots
no.t: Big cystic spots ==need many applications and may only partly flatten==.

no.title: Dark marks can linger
no.t: ==Spots can leave marks that fade slowly== rather than vanishing.

the-ordinary-100-plant-derived-squalane.bottom: A fragrance-free, light squalane oil that adds moisture to dry or reactive skin, a few drops at a time. It works with a moisturizer rather than instead of one, and too much sits greasy.

yes.title: Keeps dry skin comfortable
yes.t: A few drops over damp skin or in moisturizer ==keep skin hydrated through the day==.

yes.title: Doesn't sting or burn
yes.t: Goes on first over irritated skin ==without burning==, and rarely sets off a reaction.

yes.title: Softens flaky, treatment-dried skin
yes.t: A few drops ==smooth flaking from retinoids and other drying treatments==, mixed in or layered on top.

yes.title: Cheaper than rivals
yes.t: ==Far cheaper than Biossance's squalane==, and a few drops go a long way.

no.title: Splits opinion on oily skin
no.t: A few drops tone down shine for some, ==but extra just sits and looks oilier== on others.

no.title: Works with a moisturizer
no.t: As an oil, it ==softens skin but usually goes alongside a moisturizer==, not in place of one.

no.title: Can bring spots for a few
no.t: Spots or inflamed bumps showed up the next day for a few, ==though most skin tolerates it==.

no.title: Rare flare-ups on reactive skin
no.t: Most reactive skin copes, but ==redness and dryness can flare== for a few.

the-ordinary-aha-30-bha-2-peeling-soluti.bottom: A fragrance-free 10-minute peel with glycolic, lactic and salicylic acids, used about once a week. It leaves skin smooth and bright for many. It is strong, and burns or raw skin are common with overuse.

yes.title: Smooth, bright skin next morning
yes.t: Skin feels ==baby-smooth and looks brighter the morning after== a weekly ten-minute peel.

yes.title: Smaller bumps, smoother texture
yes.t: Closed comedones and rough patches ==look smaller and smoother over weeks of weekly use==.

yes.title: Fades marks slowly
yes.t: Dark spots and post-blemish marks ==look lighter after several weeks of weekly use==.

yes.title: Low cost for a strong peel
yes.t: ==A little goes a long way==, so one bottle covers many weekly sessions.

no.title: Stings and can burn
no.t: ==Tingles for the first minutes and can burn or leave red patches==, especially on damp skin.

tip.t: Apply to dry skin and build up from a few minutes to the full ten.

no.title: Easy to overuse
no.t: Weekly is the ceiling for many; ==extra minutes or a second weekly use left skin raw and tight==.

tip.t: Follow with a rich moisturiser the same night.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Purges or ==brings cyst-like lumps and closed comedones== for some, while others clear up.

no.title: Little change for some
no.t: ==Many see no visible change==, especially skin that already tolerates stronger acids.

the-ordinary-alpha-arbutin-2-ha.bottom: A cheap, fragrance-free serum with 2% alpha arbutin, used at night to fade dark marks. It is mild and works slowly. A minority get breakouts or dryness from it.

yes.title: Fades dark marks
yes.t: Marks from spots or scars ==look lighter after about two to three months== of nightly use.

yes.title: Mild on most skin
yes.t: Most use it nightly without redness, ==including sensitive, breakout-prone skin==.

yes.title: Plays well with other actives
yes.t: Used alongside ==niacinamide, vitamin C or benzoyl peroxide== without trouble.

no.title: Slow, modest results
no.t: ==No change for some after five weeks or more==; it is not a quick fix.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Chin and jaw bumps ==appear within a week or two== for some.

no.title: Can dry or irritate
no.t: Dryness or irritation shows up in cold, dry weather ==or on sensitive skin==.

the-ordinary-ascorbyl-glucoside-solution.bottom: A cheap, fragrance-free vitamin C serum that is gentler than most. Brightening builds slowly over weeks. It can feel sticky and pill under other layers.

yes.title: Gentle vitamin C
yes.t: A mild vitamin C that ==stays comfortable even with daily morning use== over many months.

yes.title: Evens tone over time
yes.t: Skin ==looks brighter and more even after about a month== of steady use.

no.title: Sticky, can pill
no.t: Feels ==viscous and tacky, and can ball up under moisturizer or makeup==.

tip.t: Use less and let it dry down for several minutes before the next layer.

no.title: Slow, quiet results
no.t: ==Some see little change== after a bottle, as vitamin C results are gradual.

the-ordinary-azelaic-acid-suspension-10.bottom: A low-cost, fragrance-free azelaic acid for redness, bumps and uneven tone. Results build over weeks, not days. The silicone base pills under layers and can sting at first.

yes.title: Takes the edge off redness
yes.t: Redness ==looks calmer after a month or more== of steady daily use.

yes.title: Calmer-looking bumps
yes.t: Bumps ==look smaller and fade faster== after a few weeks of use.

yes.title: Evens out leftover marks
yes.t: Red and dark spots from old breakouts ==fade slowly, over weeks==.

yes.title: Cheap way to try it
yes.t: ==A low-cost way to try azelaic acid== before a pricier version.

no.title: Pills under other layers
no.t: The silicone base ==balls up under moisturizer, oils or makeup==.

tip.t: Use less, pat it in and let it set before the next layer.

no.title: Can sting at first
no.t: Can sting or itch, ==especially in the first weeks or around the nose==.

tip.t: Start every other day and build up slowly.

no.title: Gritty, siliconey feel
no.t: Goes on ==thick and chalky==, nothing like a light serum.

no.title: Can feel drying
no.t: Can feel ==dry and powdery on bare skin==; a moisturizer under it helps.

the-ordinary-caffeine-solution-5-egcg.bottom: A fragrance-free caffeine eye serum that costs little and works best on puffy mornings. Dark circles rarely shift, and it often dries or stings the eye area.

yes.title: Shrinks morning puffiness
yes.t: Puffy mornings look ==smaller within minutes==, though the effect is short-lived.

yes.title: Slight lift for dark circles
yes.t: Shadows look ==a little lighter after a few weeks== for some; inherited circles rarely change.

yes.title: Cheap, and a bottle lasts
yes.t: ==A small bottle lasts a month or more== at a very low price.

no.title: Dries and tightens the eyes
no.t: ==Leaves the eye area dry and tight==, especially in winter or with daily use.

tip.t: Layer a moisturizer or eye cream over it once it has dried.

no.title: Stings or irritates some
no.t: Brings ==burning, redness or eye twitching== for some, often within days.

no.title: Often no change for dark circles
no.t: ==Purple-blue and inherited dark circles tend to stay== after months of use.

no.title: Can pill under makeup
no.t: Can ==ball up or flake under concealer== unless you use very little.

tip.t: Pat in one tiny drop and let it sink in before makeup.

the-ordinary-glucoside-foaming-cleanser.bottom: A fragrance-free, low-cost foaming cleanser. It cleans without leaving skin tight. Skin that dries out may find it a little tight.

yes.title: Gentle, not tight
yes.t: Cleans well and ==leaves skin soft rather than squeaky==, even when dry.

yes.title: Plain and simple
yes.t: A basic, neutral formula ==with no fragrance and no breakouts==.

no.title: Drying for a few
no.t: Left a few faces ==tight or dried out==, mainly if skin dries before serum.

the-ordinary-glycolic-acid-7-exfoliating.bottom: A cheap, fragrance-free 7% glycolic toner that smooths and brightens, and works on the body too. It is too strong for many faces, so start slowly. It stings, dries or breaks out some skin.

yes.title: Smooths and brightens
yes.t: Used a few nights a week, skin ==feels smoother and looks brighter within weeks==.

yes.title: Fades dark marks slowly
yes.t: ==Marks lighten gradually over weeks to months== of steady use, not overnight.

yes.title: Good beyond the face
yes.t: ==Smooths rough arm bumps and razor bumps== when swiped on the body after shaving.

yes.title: Big bottle, low price
yes.t: ==A large bottle that lasts for months== at a budget price.

no.title: Too strong for many faces
no.t: ==Stings, reddens or dries the face== of many, though the body usually copes better.

tip.t: Start once or twice a week and build up slowly.

no.title: Splits on breakouts
no.t: ==Bumps look calmer on some faces and more breakouts show up on others==.

no.title: Sticky finish
no.t: Takes several minutes to dry down and ==leaves a tacky film== on the face.

no.title: Misses for some
no.t: ==Texture, rough bumps and dark marks stay put== for some, even after months.

the-ordinary-glycolipid-cream.bottom: A fragrance-free cream cleanser that removes sunscreen and makeup without stripping. It suits dry and normal skin best. A few people broke out.

yes.title: Cleans without stripping
yes.t: Takes off ==sunscreen and mascara but leaves skin soft==, never tight.

yes.title: Best on dry skin
yes.t: ==A little goes a long way== as a morning or makeup-removing wash on dry skin.

no.title: Broke a few out
no.t: ==Bumps and texture appeared== for some, clearing only after stopping it.

the-ordinary-granactive-retinoid-2-emuls.bottom: A fragrance-free, low-cost retinoid emulsion, thin and quick to sink in. It suits sensitive skin and first-timers. Results are mild, and some see nothing or break out.

yes.title: Gentle first retinoid
yes.t: Even ==very reactive skin tolerated nightly use for months==, with little or no purge.

yes.title: Smoother, glowier skin
yes.t: Texture looks ==smoother and brighter within about six to eight weeks==, with softness by morning.

yes.title: Thin, easy to layer
yes.t: A runny emulsion that ==absorbs faster than the squalane version== and layers under moisturizer.

yes.title: Marks fade slowly
yes.t: Post-breakout redness and scarring look ==softer over weeks, while stubborn marks linger==.

no.title: Mild results
no.t: ==Some get no visible change after months== and step up to adapalene or tretinoin.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Whiteheads or cysts show up in ==the first weeks for a few==, often on the chin and jaw.

tip.t: Start once or twice a week and build up slowly.

no.title: Short shelf life
no.t: ==Keeps best in the fridge== once opened, as it can turn quickly.

no.title: Can still flake
no.t: Occasional ==dry flaking on dry skin==, so a moisturizer afterwards matters.

the-ordinary-granactive-retinoid-5-in-sq.bottom: A fragrance-free, oil-based retinoid serum that is gentler than retinol. It suits dry skin and people new to retinoids. The catch: the squalane base feels greasy and results come slowly.

yes.title: Easy first retinoid
yes.t: Mostly ==free of redness and peeling even used nightly==, and kinder than retinol.

yes.title: Brighter, more even look
yes.t: Tone looks ==more even and smoother after several months==, and fine lines move slowest.

yes.title: Soft, hydrating feel
yes.t: Feels ==hydrating for a retinoid==, and dry-leaning skin tolerates it all over the face.

no.title: Greasy film
no.t: ==Leaves a slick film that never fully sinks in==, even in small amounts.

no.title: Slow, modest results
no.t: Lines and marks ==barely moved after months== for some, and it sits below retinol strength.

no.title: Splits on breakouts
no.t: ==Clears whiteheads for some and brings extra nose blackheads to others== in the first weeks.

no.title: Odd smell, shelf life
no.t: Smells like ==frying oil to some and can oxidise before the bottle is finished==.

the-ordinary-hyaluronic-acid-2-b5.bottom: A cheap, fragrance-free hyaluronic acid serum that plumps skin when it is patted on very wet skin. It is tacky and pills for plenty of faces, and dry skin gets mixed results.

yes.title: Plumps and hydrates
yes.t: Under moisturizer, ==skin looks plumper and stays hydrated through cold, dry months==.

yes.title: Tacky feel has a fix
yes.t: ==A few drops on a very wet face== dry down soft; patted-dry skin turns sticky.

yes.title: Gentle for some dry skin
yes.t: Some dry, reactive skin ==copes with it twice a day==, and dry patches soften over weeks.

yes.title: Big bottle for little money
yes.t: Cheap enough to use generously, ==a large bottle costs a fraction of pricier serums==.

no.title: Pills and stays sticky
no.t: Rolls into ==white bits under moisturizer, sunscreen or makeup== and stays tacky on many faces.

tip.t: Use a couple of drops on very wet skin; extra drops are what pill.

alt.t: The INKEY List version, which pills less under other products.

no.title: Can leave dry skin tight
no.t: Even on damp skin, ==dry and sensitive skin can feel tight, itchy or no better== after a few days.

no.title: Can bring tiny bumps
no.t: ==Clusters of tiny whiteheads can appear within days== for some, fading after stopping.

no.title: Varies from bottle to bottle
no.t: Texture shifts between bottles: ==some turn thick, yellowish or foamy== and feel tackier than others.

the-ordinary-lactic-acid-10-ha.bottom: A cheap, fragrance-free 10% lactic acid serum used a few nights a week, milder than glycolic. It smooths and brightens with regular use. It tingles at first and reacts badly on a few skins.

yes.title: Gentle exfoliation
yes.t: A softer option when ==glycolic is too harsh==, and sensitive skin often copes with it.

yes.title: Smoother, brighter skin
yes.t: Skin looks ==smoother and more even after a few weeks== of regular use.

yes.title: Pores and whiteheads ease
yes.t: Pores look smaller and whiteheads ease ==within one to three weeks==, mostly on oily skin.

yes.title: Cheap for an acid serum
yes.t: A ==budget alternative to pricier lactic acid serums== that still works.

no.title: Some skins react at once
no.t: A few react from the first use, ==with irritation or a heavy, headachy feel==.

no.title: Needs easing in
no.t: Skin needs an adjustment period, ==so start once a week and wear SPF by day==.

no.title: Tingles on application
no.t: A brief tingle or sting on application, ==and a little peeling at first==.

the-ordinary-matrixyl-10-ha.bottom: A fragrance-free peptide and hyaluronic acid serum aimed at fine lines. Light and hydrating, with softer forehead lines reported, but very dry skin can react.

yes.title: Softens forehead lines
yes.t: Lines on the forehead ==look less pronounced after about a month or two== of daily use.

yes.title: Light hydration
yes.t: A thin serum layer that ==adds hydration without shine== under moisturizer.

no.title: Can dry out dry skin
no.t: On naturally dry or irritated skin it ==can leave flaking and soreness==, especially around the eyes.

no.title: Lines don't always budge
no.t: Some use it for months and ==see no change in lines==, just a hydrating layer.

the-ordinary-multi-peptide-eye-serum.bottom: A fragrance-free peptide eye serum that mostly feels gentle. Under-eyes look firmer and less puffy over weeks, but it burns or causes bumps for a few.

yes.title: Firmer, less puffy under-eyes
yes.t: Under-eyes ==look firmer and less puffy after a month or so==, mainly used in the morning.

yes.title: Gentle, doesn't dry
yes.t: Mostly ==doesn't irritate or dry the eye area==, though some skip it on retinol days.

no.title: Can sting or cause bumps
no.t: A few get ==burning or small bumps on the eyelids==.

the-ordinary-multi-peptide-ha-serum.bottom: A fragrance-free peptide and hyaluronic acid serum that works mainly as a plumping, hydrating layer. It suits dry and combination skin. Fine-line results are modest and it can feel sticky.

yes.title: Plumper, more hydrated skin
yes.t: Skin looks ==smoother and plumper within days== and feels less dehydrated.

yes.title: Gentle and retinoid-friendly
yes.t: ==No stinging or redness== reported, and it pairs easily with retinoids and acids.

yes.title: Simple everyday serum
yes.t: An easy AM or PM step that ==lasts about two months== of nightly use.

no.title: Little anti-aging payoff
no.t: After one or two bottles, ==many see no change beyond hydration==.

no.title: Tacky, can pill
no.t: Dries ==sticky and can pill== under moisturizer, especially if over-applied.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: Brings ==small closed bumps or breakouts== for a few.

the-ordinary-natural-moisturizing-factor.bottom: A fragrance-free, light gel moisturizer that suits oily and combination skin. Dry skin tends to feel tight, and it can pill under makeup.

yes.title: Light gel that sinks in
yes.t: Spreads easily and ==absorbs fast with no oily residue==, a good fit for oily and combination skin.

yes.title: Didn't clog for some
yes.t: Stayed ==clear of closed bumps on breakout-prone skin== in some routines; it clogs in others.

no.title: Dries out many skins
no.t: ==Feels tight and dry within hours==, so it often needs a richer cream on top.

tip.t: Layer a heavier cream over it, especially by day or in low humidity.

no.title: Pills under makeup
no.t: Can ==ball up under foundation or a skin tint==, mainly if you use too much.

the-ordinary-natural-moisturizing-factor.bottom: A fragrance-free, silicone-free cream that sinks in fast and finishes mostly matte. It suits normal to combination skin. The catch: it breaks some people out and is too light alone for very dry skin.

yes.title: Sits light under makeup
yes.t: A ==fast-absorbing cream that leaves a mostly matte base== for sunscreen or foundation.

yes.title: Comfort for normal to dry skin
yes.t: Leaves ==skin soft and comfortable by morning==, best with a serum or facial oil layered over it.

yes.title: Plain formula, no fragrance
yes.t: ==Fragrance-free and silicone-free==, and it agrees with some easily upset skin.

yes.title: Cheap, and a little goes far
yes.t: A small amount covers the face, so ==a tube lasts a long time==.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: ==Closed comedones and blackheads== show up for some within a week or two of daily use.

no.title: Weak on very dry skin
no.t: Feels like ==nothing on very dry skin== and needs more at night or in cold weather.

tip.t: Press a few drops of facial oil over it, or mix some into the cream.

alt.t: The richer CeraVe cream, for dry skin or winter.

no.title: Heavy or pasty for some
no.t: Can feel ==thick, sweaty or pasty on oily skin== and in hot weather.

no.title: Stings some reactive skin
no.t: ==Burning or tingling== shows up for some on a damaged barrier or after long use.

the-ordinary-niacinamide-10-zinc-1.bottom: A low-cost, fragrance-free niacinamide serum that works best on very oily skin for shine and pores. It is a gamble: it breaks many people out, stings some and pills under layers.

yes.title: Cuts oil and shine
yes.t: Very oily skin ==looks less shiny and pores look smaller== after a few weeks.

yes.title: Fades marks and redness
yes.t: Post-breakout marks and redness ==look lighter after several weeks==, though some see little change.

yes.title: Calms some breakout-prone skin
yes.t: New spots ==settle sooner for some breakout-prone skin==, usually after a slow start.

yes.title: Cheap to try
yes.t: A low price means ==a trial costs little== if it turns out not to suit you.

no.title: Frequent breakouts
no.t: Closed bumps and whiteheads ==often show up within days==, mostly around the mouth, chin and cheeks.

tip.t: Start every other day and build up slowly; some skin settles after a rough first week.

alt.t: The Inkey List version, which some moved to after this one broke them out.

no.title: Stings or reddens skin
no.t: Can sting or redden skin, ==especially neat, on dry skin or after acids==.

tip.t: Use two or three drops on damp skin, or mix a drop into your moisturizer.

no.title: Pills under other layers
no.t: It goes on sticky and ==balls up under moisturizer or sunscreen== when you use too much.

tip.t: Apply to damp skin and let it dry a few minutes before the next layer.

no.title: Can leave skin tight
no.t: Some skin ==turns dry and tight== after nightly use, so a rich moisturizer on top helps.

the-ordinary-retinal-0-2-emulsion.bottom: A fragrance-free retinaldehyde emulsion that is a step up in strength from the brand's retinols. It smooths texture and tone, but it is not a first retinoid and can stain.

yes.title: Milder than expected
yes.t: Starting at twice a week, ==three or four nights became easy with little redness or dryness==.

yes.title: Smoother, brighter skin
yes.t: Brighter by about week two, then ==smoother and more even-toned by weeks eight to nine==.

yes.title: A step up from retinol
yes.t: Results come ==a bit faster than a retinol==, a good next step once a retinol is tolerated.

yes.title: Strong results for the price
yes.t: ==Budget price for a retinal==, and the small bottle goes further than it looks.

no.title: Can irritate reactive skin
no.t: Reactive skin can ==sting or turn red even when eased in slowly==, and more so as a first retinoid.

tip.t: Start once or twice a week and follow with a ceramide moisturizer.

no.title: Not a first retinoid
no.t: Work up from a lower-strength retinol first; ==jumping straight in is where trouble starts==.

alt.t: The Ordinary Retinol 0.5% in Squalane, as the step before retinal.

no.title: Results can be slow or faint
no.t: ==No visible change after months== for some, even daily or on very oily skin.

no.title: Stains yellow
no.t: The yellow formula ==leaves marks on sheets, hands and fingernails==.

the-ordinary-retinol-0-5-in-squalane.bottom: A low-cost, fragrance-free retinol in squalane, a mid-strength step up from the 0.2% version. Many tolerate it well once built up slowly. The slick texture and breakouts put others off, and some see no change.

yes.title: Tolerated well when built up
yes.t: ==Peeling and redness stay mild== when you start weekly, then move to every other night.

yes.title: Calmer bumps for some
yes.t: ==Bumps look calmer after about 3 to 6 weeks==, often following a short purge.

yes.title: A step up from 0.2%
yes.t: Skin that handled 0.2% ==steps up to this without trouble==, and some go on to 1%.

yes.title: Brighter, smoother skin
yes.t: Glow and texture ==improve slowly over two to three months==, not weeks.

no.title: Slick, oily texture
no.t: Can ==feel greasy for hours==, enough to stick hair to your face overnight.

tip.t: Press in a few drops, or mix it into your moisturizer.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: ==Forehead and jaw bumps can appear within a week== or build up over months.

no.title: No visible change for some
no.t: Even ==two to three months of steady use== can show nothing.

no.title: Too harsh for some
no.t: ==0.5% is a lot for reactive skin==, even eased in slowly; start at 0.2% first.

the-ordinary-saccharomyces-ferment-30-mi.bottom: A fragrance-free milky toner that hydrates and exfoliates very lightly. It suits dry and normal skin, and sits well under retinoids. The texture is thin.

yes.title: Hydrating, soft after
yes.t: Skin feels ==soft and plump rather than tight==, enough that some had to change moisturizer.

yes.title: Gentle enough for tricky skin
yes.t: ==Exfoliates kindly alongside retinoids== or a stressed barrier, without redness.

no.title: Thin, easy to underwhelm
no.t: Runs almost as thin as water, and ==some notice no extra hydration or difference==.

no.title: Can flake or break out
no.t: Every-other-day use brought ==peeling for some==, and whiteheads or a heavy film on oilier skin.

the-ordinary-salicylic-acid-2-anhydrous-.bottom: A fragrance-free, oil-based salicylic acid solution for dots and bumps, applied in drops. Gentle for many, but the oily feel splits opinion.

yes.title: Kind to sensitive and dry skin
yes.t: Mostly ==comfortable on sensitive and dry skin==, with no tightness or sting.

yes.title: Bumps and plugs look smoother
yes.t: Small bumps and plugs ==loosen and look smoother within a few weeks==, as a last step.

no.title: Feels oily, blocks moisturizer
no.t: Sits as an oil, so ==moisturizer struggles to sit cleanly on top== and it can feel greasy.

no.title: Irritates or does little for some
no.t: Some get ==redness and extra pimples==, while others see no change after weeks.

the-ordinary-salicylic-acid-2-masque.bottom: A fragrance-free salicylic clay mask for oily skin, used once or twice a week. Skin feels smoother after rinsing. It dries or stings a few, and results are modest.

yes.title: Smoother, calmer after rinsing
yes.t: Skin ==feels smoother and minor breakouts calm down== after a rinse-off use.

yes.title: Gentle at weekly use
yes.t: Used weekly, ==it rarely irritates, even on sensitive skin==.

no.title: Dry, gritty, can sting
no.t: Can feel ==drying, gritty and hard to rinse off==, and stings a few.

no.title: Modest results
no.t: Smoother skin, but ==clogged pores and blackheads often stay put==.

the-ordinary-salicylic-acid-2-solution.bottom: A cheap, fragrance-free 2% salicylic acid for blackheads, whiteheads and clogged pores. Start slowly, as it reacts badly on some skin.

yes.title: Smaller blackheads and bumps
yes.t: Blackheads and small bumps ==look smaller within one to three weeks== of regular use.

yes.title: Handy on a forming pimple
yes.t: Dabbed on a forming spot, ==it dries it out overnight==.

yes.title: Thin, light liquid
yes.t: A few drops cover the face, and ==it spreads thin without sticking==.

yes.title: Cheap to run
yes.t: ==Costs a fraction of pricier BHA liquids==, and a small bottle goes far.

no.title: Rashes or burning for some
no.t: Redness, rashes or swelling ==appear within days for some==, or after months of calm use.

tip.t: Start with a few drops two or three times a week and build up.

no.title: New whiteheads can surface early
no.t: In the first week or two, ==whiteheads can surface== and look like a breakout.

no.title: Little change for some
no.t: Some skin sees ==no change after months==, especially on stubborn blackheads.

no.title: Oily nose next morning
no.t: The nose can ==look oilier the morning after==.

the-ordinary-soothing-barrier-support-se.bottom: A fragrance-free, water-light serum with barrier-support ingredients, used under moisturizer. It settles skin stressed by retinoids or exfoliants. It stings or breaks out some faces.

yes.title: Settles retinoid and exfoliant dryness
yes.t: Used with tretinoin or after over-exfoliating, ==skin looks calmer within days== and flaking eases.

yes.title: Redness looks calmer
yes.t: Visible redness ==looks calmer after about three weeks of daily use==.

yes.title: Light, fast-absorbing moisture
yes.t: Sinks in quickly, but ==very dry skin needs a cream on top==.

no.title: Burns for some
no.t: Burns or itches for a minute or longer, ==worse after a few days and under sunscreen==.

no.title: Can break out
no.t: Small pustules or breakouts ==show up within a day or two== for some.

no.title: Can pill
no.t: Layers poorly: ==it pilled on first use== for some, and left a pink film at the hairline for one.

the-ordinary-squalane-cleanser.bottom: A fragrance-free balm cleanser that melts into oil and rinses off soft and not tight. It lifts light makeup and sunscreen, but often leaves waterproof mascara behind. It breaks some people out and can leave a film.

yes.title: Gentle and non-stripping
yes.t: Skin ==feels soft and comfortable right after rinsing==, even after removing makeup.

yes.title: Melts off makeup and sunscreen
yes.t: Works best ==massaged on dry skin for a minute== before water; light makeup and sunscreen slide off.

yes.title: Comfortable on dry, reactive skin
yes.t: Dry winter skin ==feels hydrated after rinsing==, and very reactive faces tolerate it where others failed.

yes.title: Good value balm cleanser
yes.t: Fragrance-free, with ==a travel size cheap enough to try== first.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: ==Bumps can show up within a week== along the chin and hairline, even with good rinsing.

no.title: Leaves mascara behind
no.t: Light makeup lifts, but ==waterproof mascara and stubborn sunscreen need a second cleanse==.

tip.t: Follow with a water-based cleanser to pick up what's left.

no.title: Can leave a film
no.t: ==Rinses off slowly and needs a water-based wash after==, mostly on oily skin.

no.title: Tubes can turn smelly
no.t: Some tubes ==start smelling sour or like wet dog== partway through, despite normal storage.

the-ordinary-vitamin-c-suspension-23-ha-.bottom: A cheap, fragrance-free 23% vitamin C suspension in a creamy, slightly gritty base. It brightens and evens tone with steady use at night. The grit, greasy feel and sting make it harder going for beginners.

yes.title: Brightens dull skin
yes.t: Skin looks brighter within a couple of weeks, ==and dark marks lighten slowly over a month or more==.

yes.title: Mixes down easily
yes.t: Blending a few drops into moisturizer ==dissolves the grit and softens the sting==.

yes.title: High strength, budget price
yes.t: A potent vitamin C that ==stays stable and costs little== compared with pricier serums.

no.title: Gritty, greasy texture
no.t: Grainy going on and a little oily, ==so most keep it to nights== rather than under makeup.

tip.t: Mix a few drops into moisturizer to dissolve the grit.

no.title: Stings and irritates
no.t: Tingles or stings, ==more at first or when layered with a retinol==.

no.title: Pills under makeup
no.t: Rolls into balls under moisturizer or makeup, and ==the residue clings to hands for hours==.

torriden-dive-in-low-molecular-hyaluroni.bottom: A fragrance-free, watery HA serum that sinks in fast, best for dry, dehydrated and combination skin. It needs a cream over it, and it breaks a few people out.

yes.title: Sinks in with no stickiness
yes.t: ==Absorbs fast with no tacky film==, so it layers cleanly under cream, sunscreen and makeup.

yes.title: Plumps dry, dehydrated skin
yes.t: Skin looks ==plumper and less flaky within days==, and dry, dehydrated skin likes it most.

yes.title: Fragrance-free and gentle
yes.t: ==No scent and little irritation==, including for sensitive and oily skin.

yes.title: Lighter than basic HA serums
yes.t: Often ==preferred to The Ordinary's HA serum for its lighter, glassier feel==.

no.title: Needs a cream on top
no.t: ==Hydration fades without a moisturizer over it==, more so in winter or on very dry skin.

tip.t: Follow with a moisturizer to hold the hydration in.

no.title: Underwhelms some skin
no.t: ==Some skin sees no change==, like putting on a watery essence.

no.title: Breaks some people out
no.t: A few get ==tiny bumps or breakouts==, mostly with frequent use.

torriden-dive-in-mask.bottom: A fragrance-free hyaluronic sheet mask that floods skin with moisture. It suits dry, sensitive and breakout-prone skin. Oilier skin can find it heavy.

yes.title: Plumping, calming hydration
yes.t: Skin looks ==plump and soothed right after one use==, without irritation.

yes.title: Absorbs without stickiness
yes.t: The ==essence sinks in rather than sitting tacky==, and the sheet is thick enough not to dry out.

no.title: Heavy for oily skin
no.t: ==A tacky or heavy feel== on oilier skin right after.

torriden-dive-in-soothing-cream.bottom: A fragrance-free, water-light gel cream that cools and hydrates, best in warm, humid weather. Dry skin and winter need more.

yes.title: Cooling gel that sinks in
yes.t: A watery, cooling gel that ==absorbs quickly without feeling greasy==, even in humid heat.

yes.title: Hydrates without weight
yes.t: Skin feels ==hydrated and soft all day==, and post-cleanse tightness eases.

yes.title: Calm on reactive skin
yes.t: No fragrance and ==no stinging even on a sensitised face==.

yes.title: Layers under SPF and makeup
yes.t: Spreads thin and ==sits smoothly under sunscreen and makeup==.

no.title: Too light for dry air
no.t: In dry skin and cold, dry air ==cheeks turn tight or flaky== as the weather cools.

tip.t: Seal it with a richer cream or occlusive in cold weather.

no.title: Mixed for breakout-prone skin
no.t: It ==calms some breakout-prone faces and clogs others== with chin bumps or pimples.

no.title: Shiny in heat for some
no.t: Some oily skin turns ==sticky or shiny in heat==, especially with SPF over it.

torriden-dive-in-toner.bottom: A fragrance-free hyaluronic toner that is watery and light. Hydrating for many, but a few see little change.

yes.title: Light, quick hydration
yes.t: Watery and ==sinks in without residue==, with hydration that builds over layers.

no.title: Low-key effect
no.t: Splits opinion: ==no visible change== for some, and slow to soak in.

torriden-solid-in-ceramide-cream.bottom: A fragrance-free ceramide cream with a thick, buttery feel, made for dry skin and winter nights. It seals more than it hydrates, so add a serum in cold weather. Oily skin finds it heavy.

yes.title: Rich comfort for dry skin
yes.t: ==Thick, buttery moisture== that keeps very dry skin comfortable overnight.

yes.title: Sinks in better than it looks
yes.t: Thick in the tub, but it ==absorbs without a greasy finish== for most.

yes.title: Holds up over tretinoin
yes.t: A good ==winter cream over tretinoin==, keeping flaky spots under control.

yes.title: Gentle, no fragrance
yes.t: Unscented, and ==gentle on dry, sensitive skin==.

no.title: Heavy on oily skin
no.t: Leaves ==a tacky, slightly oily film== on oily skin and in humid weather.

no.title: Seals more than it hydrates
no.t: More occlusive than hydrating, so ==add a hydrating serum under it== in cold weather.

no.title: Clogs or irritates a few
no.t: A few clog-prone or reactive faces ==broke out or felt irritated==.

vanicream-daily-facial-moisturizer.bottom: A fragrance-free, lightweight lotion with ceramides and hyaluronic acid, at a drugstore price. It hydrates without a greasy feel and suits sensitive, normal and combination skin. It stings or breaks out some, and it's thin for very dry skin.

yes.title: Hydrates without grease
yes.t: A thin lotion that ==keeps skin plump all day with no sticky or oily film==.

yes.title: Easy on reactive skin
yes.t: Very reactive skin ==mostly stays calm on it==, and many return to it for years.

yes.title: Sinks in, layers well
yes.t: Absorbs fast and ==sits under sunscreen or makeup without pilling==, with no wait.

yes.title: Cheap for what it has
yes.t: A ==fraction of the price of other ceramide lotions== in a squeeze tube.

no.title: Stings some skin
no.t: ==Burns or stings in a minority==, mainly on a damaged barrier or after a fresh cleanse.

no.title: Splits breakout-prone skin
no.t: ==Keeps some faces clear and clogs others==; the reasons vary from face to face.

no.title: Too thin for very dry skin
no.t: In ==cold, dry winters it needs a richer cream== on top to last.

tip.t: Layer a richer cream over it on dry days or at night.

alt.t: The heavier Vanicream cream, for very dry skin or winter.

vanicream-facial-moisturizer-with-sunscr.bottom: A fragrance-free mineral SPF moisturizer that sensitive skin tolerates well. The texture is thick and greasy for many.

yes.title: Gentle on sensitive skin
yes.t: A ==mineral SPF that stays calm on very reactive skin==, even when other sunscreens flare it.

yes.title: Moisturizing mineral SPF
yes.t: Doubles as a moisturizer and ==sits fine under makeup== for some.

no.title: Thick and greasy finish
no.t: Feels ==thick and paste-like==, so only a small amount works.

vanicream-gentle-facial-cleanser.bottom: A fragrance-free, lightly foaming cleanser that stays cheap and plain. It suits sensitive and combination skin. The catch: it leaves some faces tight and breaks others out.

yes.title: Gentle on reactive skin
yes.t: Goes on beside tretinoin or Differin ==without stinging or stripping==, even on very fussy skin.

yes.title: Lathers lightly, rinses clean
yes.t: A modest foam that ==cleans without the squeaky, tight feel== on many faces.

yes.title: Removes everyday makeup
yes.t: Two washes ==lift daily makeup and leave no film== for most.

yes.title: Low-cost staple
yes.t: A plain basic that ==costs little and lasts a long time== in the bathroom.

no.title: Leaves some skin tight
no.t: ==Dry, combination and barrier-damaged skin== often feels stripped straight after rinsing.

tip.t: Moisturize right after rinsing and keep to a small amount of cleanser.

alt.t: CeraVe Hydrating Cleanser, a creamier wash for skin that feels stripped.

no.title: Splits on breakouts
no.t: ==Clears some faces and brings whiteheads and bumps to others==.

no.title: Stings or reddens a minority
no.t: ==Burning or redness from the first wash== shows up on some very reactive skin.

no.title: Weak on heavy makeup
no.t: ==Waterproof mascara and eyeliner need a first cleanse== with oil or micellar water.

vanicream-moisturizing-cream.bottom: A thick, fragrance-free petrolatum cream in a big tub, for dry and very reactive skin. It's a cheap barrier staple, and kind over tretinoin. It runs heavy on the face and clogs some.

yes.title: Easy on reactive skin
yes.t: A bare-bones formula that ==rarely stings==, even when skin is raw or very reactive.

yes.title: Rich moisture for dry skin
yes.t: A thick cream that ==keeps very dry skin moisturized== through winter.

yes.title: Cushions retinoid dryness
yes.t: Over tretinoin it ==keeps flaking away without stinging==.

yes.title: Big tub, low price
yes.t: ==A big tub that lasts months== and costs little.

no.title: Heavy, slow to sink in
no.t: A ==thick, occlusive feel== that sits on top and looks oily on the face.

no.title: Clogs some faces
no.t: ==Breaks some faces out== or gives comedones, mostly with longer use.

no.title: Pills under makeup
no.t: The petrolatum base ==pills or floats under sunscreen and makeup==.

no.title: Reactions for a few
no.t: Brings ==hives, rash or burning== for some sensitive skin.
